Igor Sarzyński, creative director of CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2 , has jokingly declared his own game canceled after spending time with Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto VI . The quip came two days after GTA VI launched on November 19, and a day after Take-Two announced that the game had sold 32.5 million units before release and generated $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales worldwide. Take-Two calls this the biggest entertainment launch in history, although both figures are the publisher's own estimates.

The joke does not reflect the state of the project. CD Projekt's latest update puts 184 developers on Cyberpunk 2 , and Sarzyński returned to the same thread within hours to say the studio is pursuing its own vision rather than chasing Rockstar.

In a Bluesky post published on November 21, Sarzyński wrote:

" GTAVI -induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle. Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled, imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now."

The sincere praise leading up to the punchline makes the intent clear. Rather than making any kind of announcement, Sarzyński was offering a self-deprecating salute to a rival studio whose work he plainly admires.

A few hours later, Sarzyński dropped the act and explained how his team views Rockstar's achievement. "Seriously though, I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor," he wrote. " GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed."

Sarzyński was not the first CD Projekt Red figure to congratulate Rockstar. On launch day, Cyberpunk 2 associate game director Paweł Sasko wrote on X that his first early look at the game showed Rockstar had "cooked some generational banger."

CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski followed later that day, saying Rockstar had "created a masterpiece that I am planning to explore in the coming weeks and months." He added that "it is unbelievably hard to achieve what you just did," quoting a post from the official Cyberpunk 2077 account that sent love "From Night City to Vice City."

Cyberpunk 2 entered pre-production in May 2025, the phase in which CD Projekt Red builds out its team, prototypes concepts, and settles how the game will take shape. The studio has steadily expanded the project since then, from 96 developers at the start of pre-production to 184 as of July 31, 2026, according to its H1 2026 earnings report. CD Projekt has not yet announced a move into full production.

CD Projekt Red is not sweeping leaves any time soon, but fans should expect a long wait. The company has said Cyberpunk 2 will not launch before 2028, and Nowakowski has noted that the studio's journey from pre-production to release takes four to five years on average. If that pattern holds, a release around 2029 or 2030 looks more realistic, although CD Projekt has not committed to any date.

Ignor Sarzynski – Bluesky | Pawel Sasko – X | Michal Nowakowski – X

items.title: “We Might as Well Cancel It”: Cyberpunk 2 Director Says GTA 6’s Quality and Open World Left the Development Team Depressed
items.summary: CD Projekt RED knows it faces a major challenge with the sequel, as Rockstar has raised the bar for sandbox games
items.content:

Beyond the debate surrounding reviews and its rivalry with other legendary franchises, those who have already played Grand Theft Auto VI agree that it is one of the best video games ever made. Its achievements have pushed open-world games toward a new standard.

This is certainly a major compliment for Rockstar Games, but it also represents a challenge and added pressure for open-world games coming out in the years ahead.

One of them is Cyberpunk 2 , the sequel to CD Projekt RED’s troubled 2020 release. The game now faces an even greater challenge as it tries to meet the standard set by Rockstar Games.

Back in the days of GTA: Vice City , one review described the game as a new frontier for video games and humanity, given the impact it had beyond the industry. In gaming, GTA 6 has achieved something similar in an era when players have extremely high expectations thanks to technological advancements.

Igor Sarzyński, director of Cyberpunk 2 , acknowledged in a BlueSky post that Rockstar Games’ latest release has put considerable pressure on other open-world projects currently in development:

“GTA 6-induced open-world game development depression is real. It’s probably the greatest artistic achievement in history given its scale, density, coherence, and it’s a technological and creative miracle.”

The creative director later joked about the future of his game: “Cyberpunk 2 is canceled, I’m going to sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now.”

Although Cyberpunk is a different beast, especially since it is a role-playing game, comparisons between the hype leading up to its release and the actual results are inevitable.

At the time, Cyberpunk 2077 promised that Night City would be a living, detailed city where players could visit every location and their actions would have consequences. In December 2020, it became clear that this was not the case. Although the game is now in great shape, it failed to live up to its own hype.

Meanwhile, Rockstar Games worked quietly for almost a decade and, on November 19, delivered a game that redefined open worlds, something the studio had already accomplished years earlier with Red Dead Redemption 2 .

Now, Cyberpunk 2 carries the stigma of its predecessor’s disastrous launch. However, CD Projekt RED has made the necessary adjustments to avoid a repeat of that tragedy, including having creative team members live full-time near the studio’s Boston office so they can immerse themselves in North American culture. Of course, all of this happened before GTA 6 changed everything.

items.title: Is There A Point Of No Return Before The 18 ‘GTA 6’ Endings?
items.summary: 'GTA 6' has more than a dozen possible endings, but before you choose any of them, is there a point of no return in the game?
items.content:
Gaming Is There A Point Of No Return Before The 18 ‘GTA 6’ Endings? Forbes Follow Paul Tassi, Senior Contributor Updated Tue, November 24, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC Updated Tue, November 24, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC figure]:grid max-md:[&>figure]:grid-cols-article-mobile max-md:[&>figure>*]:col-fullbleed max-md:[&>figure>figcaption]:col-body"> *]:pointer-events-auto hidden md:block"> GTA 6

Any Cyberpunk 2077 player knows the phrase "Meet Hanako at Embers." It's the final prompt before you enter into the ending of the game, which can go one of a half dozen ways depending on your choices and during the upcoming finale. As I played Grand Theft Auto 6 , I wondered if we were going to get into the same situation in the game, or if Rockstar was going to pull a Red Dead Redemption 2 in some way, finishing the story but having players keep going afterward after one of GTA 6's 18 endings. Yes, there are 18 ending variants that have been discovered so far.

There is, in fact, a Meet Hanako at Embers for GTA 6 . It's the mission "Meet with Abe," which is described as (spoilers) finalizing your deal and that "there's no going back" once you sign. As you head into the building, you are given obvious prompts that this is the end, though you can choose to get some more stuff done before you head there. Depending on the ending you want, I highly recommend doing enough stuff to hit $2 million in your BuckMe.

After you get your ending, (and do not ask me how to get all of the 18 discovered endings because I have no idea for like 15 of them), this is the place in time that you will be dropped back into the world to keep playing the game, which is exactly how Cyberpunk 2077 plays out. You can go back and get at least some of the endings with new choices, but other things involve your money, your criminal profile, your relationship status, and more, so you may have to work to change those, or it may just be time to start another playthrough, as many did in Cyberpunk .

From there, once you hit $2 million in your BuckMe, everything you get past that will just be spending money. There are, unfortunately, no hugely big-ticket items like more safehouses or businesses to buy this time around, so it's mostly clothes, guns and cars. The single biggest purchase I've made was $86,000 to register a rare Vitello supercar. I think the Thrax, which I haven't found, is likely more than that. But even still, you will run out of purchases eventually.

That doesn't mean there's not more fun to be had as there are a zillion things to do and find as you make your way toward 100% completion. Once you hit 100% in the story, the percent will change to your overall game percentage. After my ending, I was at 72%. I've probably played for 30 more hours since then, and I am now at 78%. It's slow going, but the game has a checklist of what you should focus on. Have fun!

items.title: GTA 6 Leaves Cyberpunk 2 Director Impressed
items.summary: The launch of Grand Theft Auto and its success, both in sales and reviews, is intimidating developers working on future open-world games, especially those set in cities. This includes the CD Projekt…
items.content:
The launch of Grand Theft Auto and its success, both in sales and reviews, is intimidating developers working on future open-world games, especially those set in cities. This includes the CD Projekt team working on the sequel to Cyberpunk 2077 .

The truth is that Cyberpunk 2 and GTA 6 are different in many ways: one is an action RPG that offers great freedom when approaching situations and making decisions that affect the story, while the other is an action-adventure game with enormous interactivity. However, every game developer knows that Rockstar Games’ title will set the standard for future open-world games in terms of graphics, map density, missions, and system complexity.

seriously though i think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor. GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed

Igor Sarzynski, creative director of Cyberpunk 2, has expressed his anxiety after seeing what GTA 6 has achieved. Although CD Projekt will release The Witcher 4 first , the science-fiction RPG will take place in a large city, meaning comparisons between the two games will become much more common.

“GTAVI-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real,” he commented on Bluesky. “probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, i mean it. scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle.” In a joking tone, he says that Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled and that he will spend his time sweeping the autumn leaves in his backyard.

In a second message, while speaking “seriously”, he points out that his game has a “unique” touch, meaning it would not be fair to compare it directly with GTA. “GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed.”

Little is known about this sequel because the studio’s priority is its next The Witcher game. We do know, however, that next Cyberpunk will make the move to Unreal Engine 5, like other projects from the studio, and that it will take place in a city inspired by Chicago. A new studio has also been established in Boston to develop the game, with support from Vancouver. In the past, its release has been estimated for late 2030 or 2031, although Cyberpunk 2077 suffered several delays that could also happen with this sequel.

As more information becomes available, we’ll make sure to let you guys know here at eTeknix

items.content:
‘Cyberpunk 2’ is expected to be released between 2029 and 2030

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

The creative director of Cyberpunk 2 has joked that the upcoming game should be cancelled after seeing what Rockstar Games has achieved with Grand Theft Auto VI.

Igor Sarzyński, who is leading development on the sequel at CD Projekt Red , took to social media to praise the newly released GTA 6 , describing it as “probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history”.

In a post on Bluesky on Saturday, Sarzyński wrote: “GTA VI-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle.”

He then added, jokingly: “Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled, imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now.”

His comments prompted a response from Cyberpunk 2 lead writer Anna Megill, who replied: “But wait.”

Sarzyński was quick to reassure fans that the project was still moving forward, however, explaining that CD Projekt Red was working on something with its own identity.

“Seriously though, I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor,” he continued. “GTA is impressive in a way all great art is: it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed.”

GTA 6 launched on November 19 and has been widely praised for its enormous open world and attention to detail. The game has also enjoyed an extraordinary commercial debut, with estimated retail sales of $3.79bn in its first 24 hours, according to reports.

Cyberpunk 2, meanwhile, is still in development at CD Projekt Red and is not expected for release until 2029 or 2030, according to Metro .

Cyberpunk 2077 was released in December 2020 after years of enormous anticipation. The open-world RPG was praised by critics for its ambitious storytelling, characters and richly detailed world.

However, its launch was overshadowed by widespread technical problems, including game-breaking bugs, frequent crashes and poor performance on PlayStation 4 and Xbox One.

items.title: 7 Long Open-World RPGs That Take Forever to Complete
items.summary: Open-world games like Cyberpunk 2077 will keep players busy for 100 hours or more.
items.content:
Image via CD Projekt Red Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Sage Negron Published Nov 23, 2026, 7:30 PM EST Sage Negron is a freelance writer based in New York City. He has contributed to CBR in the past, as well as Looper and DualShockers. When he's not writing, he's usually playing video games or reading a good book. Sign in to your CBR account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap One of the many reasons open-world RPGs are so popular is that they can keep players busy for dozens of hours or more. Games are often on the long side even if players focus on the main story, and if players delve into optional content like side quests and collectibles, it'll keep them busy for much longer.

Games like Cyberpunk 2077 can potentially keep players busy for hundreds of hours, making them a worthwhile investment even if players buy them at full price. Best of all, many of these games have mods that expand the original experience even more, so players could potentially play and enjoy them forever.

The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind Image via Bethesda Game Studios One of the things that makes every game in the Elder Scrolls series such fun is the fact that each game allows the player to do however they please. If they want to follow the main story, they can do so. But if they want to go off and explore the world , then they will not be punished for their actions.

The third entry, Morrowind , perfectly embodies this philosophy. The open world is jam-packed with factions to meet and side quests to complete, all of which help players level up and experiment with new armor and weapons builds. Even with all of this in the base game, two expansions and even more locations and monsters to discover, making Morrowind one of the biggest games ever.

V in a car chase with police in Cyberpunk 2077 Image via CD PROJEKT RED The main narrative of Cyberpunk 2077 , which revolves around a mercenary trying to stop their death at the hands of a chip in their brain containing the memories of a former rock star, is not a long story. Players can go through all the story missions in roughly 20 hours. But exploring everything that Night City has to offer will take much longer.

There is always a new side mission for V to undertake , or a new gig that can earn them some extra cash in one of the city's many districts. And performing these tasks will allow V to purchase new weapons, vehicles, and hideouts scattered across the map. Both the main game and the Phantom Liberty expansion will keep players busy for a very long time.

Arc Hunter in Destiny 2 Image via Bungie It was recently announced that Destiny 2 would not be receiving any more content updates, leaving behind nearly a decade's worth of gameplay modes for players to experience. It's the end of an era for the MMORPG FPS game, but that doesn’t mean that new or returning players won’t have anything to do.

These open world RPGs feel like classic game titles, but they're built for the modern age of PC gaming perfectly.

With each new year, new story expansions were introduced that added new lore to the franchise, alongside new missions, raids, gear, and modes ranging from PvP to PvE. Since Destiny 2 will still remain playable for the foreseeable future, players will have plenty of time to finish everything that these expansions have to offer, which could take hundreds of hours to even scratch the surface of.

Image via Lo-Fi Games The length of time it takes to complete Kenshi depends entirely on how much time the player is willing to put into it. The real-time strategy RPG isn’t built around a traditional story. Instead, all the player has to do is survive in a post-apocalyptic world while dealing with hostile NPCs and even more hostile environmental conditions, and that is easier said than done.

Not only is leveling up the player character very time-consuming, but the world will throw everything it can at the player to stop their progress. Factions can attack the player, weather conditions can halt the progress of resource management and exploration, and getting attacked can cause players to lose their limbs. Kenshi is the start of a long and painful story of survival.

items.title: “A masterpiece”: Cyberpunk’s co-CEO congratulates Rockstar on GTA 6
items.summary: CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski has congratulated Rockstar on Grand Theft Auto VI, calling it a masterpiece while saying he plans to spend the
items.content:
This article needs JavaScript to display. Please turn on JavaScript in your browser and reload the page. CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski has congratulated Rockstar on Grand Theft Auto VI , calling it a masterpiece while saying he plans to spend the coming weeks and months exploring it.

His November 19 message praised the people who made the game and acknowledged how difficult an achievement like that can be. It is a warm launch-day response from the company behind Cyberpunk 2077 and The Witcher .

Nowakowski's comment is a congratulatory message, not a detailed review. He did not say he had completed the game; in fact, he wrote that he intended to explore it over a longer period.

Vice City is part of GTA VI’s fictional state of Leonida. Image: Rockstar Games

The CD Projekt executive shared a launch-day greeting from the official Cyberpunk 2077 account. That message played on the names of the two games' cities and congratulated Rockstar.

Lucia and Jason are GTA VI’s two protagonists. Image: Rockstar Games

Other CD Projekt developers joined in. Paweł Sasko , associate game director on the next Cyberpunk , praised an early look at the game, while The Witcher 4 director Sebastian Kalemba said he was looking forward to spending a weekend with it.

It is easy to see why people connect the games: both Cyberpunk 2077 and GTA VI ask players to spend time in a detailed fictional setting. They are still different games, with different stories and design goals, so a launch-day compliment is best read as appreciation between developers rather than a judgment about which one is better.

GTA VI launched on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19. Image: Rockstar Games

GTA VI launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19. The following day, Take-Two estimated $3.79 billion in first-day retail sales. That figure is the publisher's sales estimate, not a count of players.

Rockstar's story follows Jason and Lucia in Leonida, a fictional state that includes Vice City. The publisher describes them as a couple drawn into a conspiracy after a job goes wrong. Nowakowski did not single out a particular mission or character in his message.

For anyone considering the boxed PS5 edition , there is a practical detail to check: it contains a download code, not a disc. Amazon's listing specifies a US or Canadian PlayStation account for redemption and marked the item non-returnable when checked.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2 creative director says he's suffering from 'GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression,' jokes that 'Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled'
items.content:
a]:text-inherit [&>a]:underline"> When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Rockstar; CD Projekt) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter It's been a big week for videogames—or rather, videogame. Grand Theft Auto 6 is enjoying what may very well be the single greatest media launch in history, securing over $3.7 billion in launch sales. But as Rockstar enjoys its acclaim, other developers—like Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski—are professing some anxiety about releasing their own games in a post-GTA 6 world.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle," Sarzynski said on Bluesky over the weekend, joking that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled."

That news came as a surprise to Cyberpunk 2 lead writer Anna Megill, who replied with a baffled "But wait—"

Sarzynski was, of course, just goofing. But I'm sympathetic to any game dev who might be feeling an amount of apprehension about being measured against GTA 6's success, particularly when there's a genre overlap.

In Cyberpunk 2's case, however, CD Projekt is very much in its own lane: Cyberpunk is a different thematic setting, with entirely different systems and design goals. I'd hope that any reasonable person would think comparing the two is like comparing apples and oranges—particularly when the oranges reportedly had a production budget upwards of $1 billion .

'I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind': Warren Spector congratulates Rockstar on its landmark accomplishment but says the industry can't keep this up 'I feel like we've built a pyramid on Everest' says Rockstar of GTA 6 meeting impossible expectations 'AAA is under the most amount of threat': Ex-Take Two boss explains why making big games is unsustainable—except for GTA 6 In a follow-up post , Sarzynski acknowledged that each project is doing its own thing, while noting that GTA 6's example will benefit other game developers by serving as a source of creative inspiration.

"Seriously though, I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor," he said. "GTA is impressive in a way all great art is: It expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed."

items.title: 11 Open World Games With Virtually Perfect Worlds
items.summary: A look at a number of titles that manage to capture the attention of players with their game worlds
items.content:
By Caitlyn Taylor Published Nov 21, 2026, 4:00 AM EST Polygon Lists A look at a number of titles that manage to capture the attention of players with their game worlds

Image: Capcom Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Sign in to your Polygon.com account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Everyone loves a fictional world to get lost in, and open-world games are some of the best ways to give gamers that experience . In the past decade, advancements within the gaming industry have expanded the capabilities of virtual worlds. Previously, gamers often had to travel between hub worlds broken apart by loading screens, but now it's far more common for gamers to travel seamlessly. Outside of sheer size, modern virtual game worlds also offer players a plethora of features and mechanics to sink their teeth into for fuller immersion. Whether you like to search every nook and cranny of a game world for unique items or follow NPCs around, the 11 games listed below have worlds players can easily get lost in.

Image: Everstone Studio/NetEase Games via Polygon Where Winds Meet wowed the industry with its unique Wuxia setting and expansive game world where travel is seamless. Set in 10th-century China during the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms era, the world of Where Winds Meet is filled with more than 150 hours of solo content for players to sink their teeth into, not to mention multiplayer features, including seamless co-op, dungeons, and joining martial sects and guilds. Additionally, Where Winds Meet's NPCs’ personalities and reactions, as well as the game’s social system , can change based on player reputation.

Image: WeirdCo Following a troubled launch, Cyberpunk 2077 has gradually rebuilt its reputation and is now considered by many within the industry to have one of modern gaming’s most immersive worlds. The world of Night City is split up into six distinct regions, which can be explored through main story content, side quests, gigs, and other events . Despite being compact, the world of Night City is dense with environmental storytelling and hidden lore that the player can seek out. Overall, while it takes around 27 hours to complete the main story, a completionist run can easily go over 100 hours.

Guerrilla Games/Sony Interactive Entertainment The world of Horizon Zero Dawn is nothing to scoff at. Players are thrust 1,000 years into a post-apocalyptic United States, now populated by tribal societies, lush flora, and prowling ancient animalistic machines. With a main story that takes only 23 hours to finish, Horizon Zero Dawn is more focused on its narrative than on being a sprawling open-world sandbox. That said, players can get lost in its intricate environment and engage with its dynamic hunting, trapping, and combat mechanics. Including side content, Horizon Zero Dawn can be completed in around 45 hours.

Image: Nintendo EPD/Nintendo Few entries have been more genre-redefining than the Zelda franchise's iconic entries: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom . Both games tap into the nostalgic history of the Zelda franchise while also breaking new ground. Breath of the Wild was the series' first modern entry to have a fully open-world setting, and it captivated players with its seamless traversal and non-linear exploration. Additionally, players were able to spend additional time thanks to the game's engaging survival and crafting mechanics as well as its physics engine, allowing players to find creative ways of solving puzzles and combat. Tears of the Kingdom only expands on the world, letting players traverse areas in the sky and underground.

Image: Rockstar Games The world of Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2 still holds up incredibly well. Set in the declining American Wild West, Red Dead Redemption 2 has an engaging and heart-wrenching story and a setting that's easy to get lost in. The game's moral honor system, which is based entirely on player actions, can shape a player's experience. Additionally, the game's extensive crafting, hunting mechanics, and random encounters can easily get players lost within its world. In its base game, Red Dead Redemption 2' s main story can take up to 60 hours to finish, but its side content can push playtime easily past 100 hours.

Image: Insomniac Games/Sony Interactive Entertainment Marvel's Spider-Man 2 is an unlikely entry but well-deserved on this list. Despite being a largely story-driven game, it's often credited as having the best virtual depiction of New York City ever made. Traversing seamlessly through the landscape of NYC has always been a staple of Spider-Man games, and Marvel's Spider-Man 2 perfected it. Its world is divided into 14 distinct districts and includes locations such as Brooklyn and Queens, along with side activities like crime reports, photo ops, Prowler caches, and mystery side missions.

Project zomboid Daytime Gameplay Firefight Image: The Indie Stone There's no better thrilling zombie experience than in Project Zomboid . This isometric open-world sandbox throws the player into a world set in fictionalized Knox County, Kentucky. The player can seamlessly traverse the map with no load times and fully non-linear gameplay. There is no set goal or story campaign; it's entirely up to the player how they survive and what they craft, in a world that gradually changes as the apocalypse deepens. As a result, a Project Zomboid playthrough lasts as long as a player can survive.

Image: Warhorse Studios/Deep Silver via Polygon The world of Kingdom Come: Deliverance and its sequel is as expansive as it is historically accurate. This series takes the player into a recreation of 1403 Bohemia within the Holy Roman Empire. Outside of combat, the game's NPCs have daily schedules and routines, including jobs, patrols, and daily activities. Additionally, the NPCs are reactive to player action, reputation, and even to how a player wears their clothes. Traversing through the world on foot, by horse, or via fast travel can lead to random encounters, making it feel very lived in.

Image: Capcom Capcom's long-awaited Dragon's Dogma sequel produced some well-received improvements to its world compared to the first game. The world of Dragon's Dogma 2 is four times the size of its predecessor. Players can traverse through this world, whether on foot or by cart, and get disrupted by dynamic monster and weather encounters that make no trip feel the same. Fast travel is easier thanks to the reusable Eternal Ferrystone, which connects players to Portcrystals. Additionally, the recent Dragons Dogma 2: Dark Arisen DLC added the northern region of Norgan , which features a wintry landscape, alongside 12 new dungeons across the game map.

The world of Crimson Desert is a selling point in and of itself, featuring a continent made up of five different countries with a variety of biomes and unique art direction that encourages players to explore. Players can choose between a variety of traversal options, including foot, gliders, land mounts, and even sea travel above and underwater. The world is populated with NPCs that follow daily routines and can travel between towns. Players can even romance a number of NPCs thanks to the recent "Charting the Unknown" DLC .

items.title: From the Anime to the Game — Free Update Brings Edgerunners 2 Content and More to Cyberpunk 2077!
items.summary: The free Edgerunners 2 Update to Cyberpunk 2077 is available now, with content inspired by the second installment of the hit anime series now streaming on Netflix
items.content:
“Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2” premiered on Netflix on October 20, bringing a whole new cast of characters to Night City for a dark, gritty ride. And now we’re bringing a little piece of that story into Cyberpunk 2077 , too! The free Edgerunners 2 Update is here, with content inspired by the anime, new ways to fight, more customization options, and plenty of other additions.

We’ve got a lot to cover, so let’s get into it. And don’t worry if you haven’t watched the new anime yet — no “Edgerunners 2” spoilers ahead!

One of the things we love about Night City is that there’s always another story unfolding somewhere. V may be central to the events of Cyberpunk 2077 , but they’re hardly the only merc in town, fighting to survive and make a name for themselves on those neon-soaked streets. Every fixer has clients, every crew has gigs to take care of, every Night City merc has their story — and sometimes, those stories collide in unexpected ways.

That’s exactly what happens in the brand-new quest introduced with the “Edgerunners 2” Update. What begins as just another gig from Wakako turns into an action-packed, high-stakes mission that sees V cross paths with Weak Kingsley, a famed Night City merc and one of the main characters of “Edgerunners 2.” We won’t spoil what happens, but during the course of this mission, V has a chance to assist Weak and his crew during a risky gig that takes place in a brand-new location: Night City Prison.

The new “Edgerunners 2” gig is more than a chance to encounter characters from the anime in the game — it serves as a prequel to the events of the series. So, play the quest before watching the anime, and you’ll have a little extra context going into Episode 1. Already seen the show? Then with this gig, you’ll get to revisit part of Weak’s story with a broader perspective of him and his crew.

And there’s even more forEdgerunnersfans in this update. For starters, you can find and equip Weak’s full outfit — vest, glasses, coat, pants, the works — and get your hands on his signature revolver, Coronation. We’ve also added a new radio station, HKGN 102.FM, featuring official tracks from both “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners” and “Edgerunners 2.” So if you’re planning to spend a few more hours cruising around Night City after watching the show, we’ve got your soundtrack covered.

What’s better than blasting your way through a warehouse full of gangoons with a revolver, dealing one headshot after another? Doing it with two revolvers, obviously.

That’s right — dual wielding is here! With the Edgerunners 2 Update, you can raise hell with a pistol or revolver in each hand. That’s a whole new vibe — and a whole new level of awesome.

But dual wielding isn’t just about looking cool. It brings a new playstyle and a fresh way to approach combat — in fact, it’s one of the most significant gameplay additions to the game’s combat since Update 2.0 introduced throwing knives. So if you’ve been looking for an excuse to shake up your fighting style, this might just be it.

Cyberware enhances your stats and abilities — but what if it could take your style to the next level, too? That’s where glamdocs come in. These new vendors let you customize the appearance of your cyberware, with 40 styles in different colors to choose from. Fancy a new look for your chrome? Pay them a visit at one (or all) of the five locations across Night City and see what catches your eye.

In a city that lives and dies by appearances, V really can’t afford to pass up any opportunity to shake up their look. On top of cyberware customization, we’ve also added 20 new hairstyles and several clothing sets to give your V the best chance of standing out, even in Night City.

We know how creative the Cyberpunk 2077 community can be, and we’re always curious to see what players come up with. That’s why we’re introducing cross-platform mod support through mod.io integration.

The update adds a Mods panel where you can browse and install supported community-created content directly in the game. It’s a new way to experiment with your experience, and we’re looking forward to seeing how it develops as more mods become available and receive support over time!

We’ve covered some of the bigger additions, but there’s still plenty to find in the Edgerunners 2 Update.

items.title: Check out what's coming to Cyberpunk 2077 in the Edgerunners 2 Update!
items.summary: Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you! Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watc
items.content:
Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you!

Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watch the Features Overview video to see some of the new features in action:

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.

    [/*]

  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.

    [/*]

  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

    [/*]

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:

    • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China

      [/*]

    • Jinguji: available in City Center

      [/*]

    • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown

      [/*]

    • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside

      [/*]

    • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.

    [/*]

  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.

    [/*]

  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.

    [/*]

  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

    [/*]

Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”
